question: Should ClawHub allow post-publish changelog edits for skill and package versions, and what authorization, audit-log, and edit-history policy should govern them?
rationale: The requested command changes public release metadata after publication, which is both product behavior and a trust boundary; source inspection shows no existing approved policy to infer safely.

options.title: Add audited owner/staff edits
options.body: Allow authorized publishers and staff to edit changelogs while recording audit metadata, preserving edit history, and synchronizing latest-version summaries.

options.title: Keep changelogs immutable
options.body: Document that release changelogs are immutable after publish and require a replacement version for corrections.

options.title: Limit to staff-only corrections
options.body: Permit only moderator/admin corrections for exceptional cases, leaving publishers on the current publish-new-version workflow.

recommendation.title: Add audited owner/staff edits
recommendation.body: Allow authorized publishers and staff to edit changelogs while recording audit metadata, preserving edit history, and synchronizing latest-version summaries.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest current-history owner for the CLI and publish backend surfaces that would enforce the policy.
